title: Erasing a finite tape segment
statement: Let $z$ be a Boolean word, let $q$ and $d$ be machine states, and choose one of the two work tapes, indexed by $k$. Suppose that for every input symbol and every pair of scanned work-tape symbols, the transition in state $q$ leaves the input head, output, and tapes unchanged, moves both work heads left when tape $k$ is occupied, and moves both right and enters state $d$ when tape $k$ is blank. If tape $k$ is occupied at every integer cell $c$ with $0\le c<h_0$, and blank at cell $-1$, then starting with both work heads at $h_0-1$ in state $q$, after $h_0+1$ steps the machine is in state $d$ with both work heads at zero; the input position, tapes, and output are unchanged. This holds for every natural number $h_0$ and either setting of the exactness parameter.
hypotheses_covered: $k$ is one of the two work-tape indices
the transition-function condition holds for every input symbol and scanned-tape tuple
tape $k$ is occupied at every natural-number cell below $h_0$
